title: Website Returns HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout
symptom: Clients experience 60+ second page loading delay followed by '504 Gateway Time-out'.
initial_observations: Reverse proxy or ALB accepts client connection, but backend fails to respond before timeout.
environment: Application behind Application Load Balancer or Nginx reverse proxy.

possible_causes.cause: Backend application blocked on slow database query or external API call
possible_causes.evidence_needed: DB slow query log or high DB CPU; app threads stuck in I/O wait.
possible_causes.remediation: Optimize slow SQL queries, add database indexes, or introduce caching layer (Redis).

possible_causes.cause: Backend thread pool saturation / high CPU starvation
possible_causes.evidence_needed: High CPU utilization (>95%) or worker queue overflow.
possible_causes.remediation: Scale backend instances horizontally or increase worker concurrency.

investigation_steps.title: Check Backend CPU, Memory, and Thread Saturation
investigation_steps.explanation: Evaluate if instance is CPU or memory saturated.
investigation_steps.what_to_look_for: High load average or CPU steal/wait.

investigation_steps.title: Inspect Proxy Upstream Response Time Logs
investigation_steps.what_to_look_for: Upstream response times exceeding proxy timeout.

prevention: Implement request timeouts at application layer lower than proxy idle timeout.
Add circuit breakers for external downstream calls.
